questions.stem: The task is to work out the following. Which sort has O(n^2) worst case but O(n) best case on nearly sorted data?

options.misconception: selection sort is O(n^2) even on sorted input

questions.explanation: Insertion sort fits all the stated constraints; each alternative fails one of them, whether stability, worst-case time, or auxiliary space. Matching every clause of the question to a known property avoids picking a sort that satisfies only part of it.
questions.hint: Check stability, worst-case time, and space separately for each candidate.

adds an extra term as if two base cases overlapped
advances the recurrence by one index too far

subtracts one per union without checking whether endpoints were already connected

off by one above the depth by counting the empty final interval

questions.stem: Solve the problem that follows. A dynamic array starts with capacity 8 and doubles its capacity whenever it is full. After 58 append operations, how many element copies have occurred in total?

options.misconception: assumes exactly one resize of the initial capacity occurs
counts only the m insertions and ignores every resize copy
overestimates by imagining a copy on every append

questions.explanation: Resizes happen when size reaches capacity; the copied amounts are 8, 16, and so on up to the last resize, summing to 56. Because each element is copied at most once per doubling level, the total is below 2m, giving amortized O(1) per append.
questions.hint: Track size and capacity together; a resize copies the current size, then capacity doubles.

questions.stem: Consider this particular instance. For an input of size n = 8185, what is the worst-case auxiliary space (excluding the input) used by a single iterative loop over the input?

counts one stack frame or buffer slot per input element
mixes the time bound of a sort into its space bound

questions.explanation: Auxiliary space counts extra memory beyond the input. For a single iterative loop over the input the dominant extra allocation grows as O(1); call-stack frames or a temporary buffer scale with that quantity, and this measure is distinct from the algorithm's running time.
questions.hint: Separate time from space: ask how deep the recursion goes or how large the extra buffer is.
